exact_boundary.single_move: Replace deterministic interpretation of one squared finite transform with an explicitly normalized estimator of the two-sided PSD of a declared WSS process, then evaluate raw-periodogram bias/variance and Welch's resolution-variance-overlap tradeoff.
exact_boundary.opening_input: The predecessor's final exercise fixed N=64, periodic Hann, L=1024, one interior bin, and 50 seeded white-noise realizations; its raw squared magnitudes had mean 0.021767896, sample SD 0.024899643, and CV 1.143870026. Reuse this only as the motivating empirical failure: padding sampled each realization more densely but did not average realizations.
required_argument_order: Distinguish an ensemble random process from one realization and state WSS before forming a PSD.
Define autocorrelation and the PSD transform pair under one sign and integration convention; verify unit-variance white noise.
Form a finite biased sample autocorrelation and connect its correlogram to the rectangular periodogram without equating sample average and expectation.
Separate periodogram bias from persistent variance; asymptotic unbiasedness does not imply consistency.
Define a window-power-normalized modified periodogram and Welch average; vary segment length and quantify resolution/CV.
Show that overlapped frames are correlated evidence, so frame count is not independent-average count.
Close by retaining frames in order as the information Welch discards.
must_not_expand_into: Re-deriving DFT/DTFT, FFT factorization, zero-padding interpolation, coherent gain, ENBW, window endpoint conventions, or deterministic close-tone resolution.
STFT time-frequency localization, spectrogram design, COLA/WOLA, synthesis windows, reconstruction, or subband/filter-bank interpretation.
AR, MUSIC, Capon, multitaper, Blackman-Tukey design, confidence-band theory, or general nonstationary spectral estimation beyond a short boundary note.

handoff.established_here: Welch averages normalized windowed periodograms across frames to estimate a stationary PSD, trading segment-length resolution for lower variance while overlap reduces effective independence.
handoff.left_open: Welch discards frame order and therefore cannot locate spectral change; the next lesson keeps X[ell,k], chooses time hop and endpoint padding, and adds COLA/WOLA reconstruction.
handoff.hard_limit: Do not teach that Welch overlap must satisfy COLA. Uniform analysis weighting may motivate a hop, but exact synthesis is a different next-lesson contract.

stochastic_and_sample_conventions.process: x[n] is one realization of a discrete-time random process. WSS means mu_x=E{x[n]} is constant and r_xx[ell]=E{x[n+ell]x*[n]} depends only on ell. Strict stationarity is stronger and is not required.
stochastic_and_sample_conventions.mean: Core formulas assume zero mean or a declared known mean removed. If a sample mean/detrend is removed, state it and acknowledge the additional finite-record bias; a nonzero mean otherwise contributes a DC spectral line.
stochastic_and_sample_conventions.ergodicity: WSS alone does not license replacing E{.} by a time average. Ergodicity/mixing is the extra modeling bridge; every finite sample quantity remains an estimator.
stochastic_and_sample_conventions.autocorrelation_pair: r_xx[ell]=E{x[n+ell]x*[n]}; r_xx[-ell]=r_xx*[ell]. S_xx(exp(j omega))=sum_ell r_xx[ell]exp(-j omega ell), and r_xx[ell]=(1/(2 pi)) integral_{-pi}^{pi} S_xx(exp(j omega))exp(j omega ell)domega.
stochastic_and_sample_conventions.sample_autocorrelation: For 0<=ell<N, use the biased estimate rhat_b[ell]=(1/N)sum_{n=0}^{N-1-ell}x[n+ell]x*[n], mirror by conjugate symmetry, and state zero outside available lags. The unbiased alternative divides by N-ell but has noisier high lags and its correlogram need not remain nonnegative.
stochastic_and_sample_conventions.periodogram_link: For a rectangular length-N record, the DTFT of rhat_b is exactly Ihat_N(omega)=|sum_{n=0}^{N-1}x[n]exp(-j omega n)|^2/N. This equality is between two finite-record estimators, not between a realization and the ensemble PSD.
stochastic_and_sample_conventions.welch: Let M be segment/window length, R hop, L>=M FFT length, K=1+floor((N_total-M)/R), U=sum_{n=0}^{M-1}|w[n]|^2, X_m[k]=sum_n w[n]x[n+mR]exp(-j2 pi kn/L), P_m[k]=|X_m[k]|^2/U, and Shat_W[k]=(1/K)sum_m P_m[k]. L controls only frequency-grid sampling; M and w[n] control smoothing/resolution.
stochastic_and_sample_conventions.overlap: Overlapping frames share samples. Their normalized window inner product rho_w[R]=sum_n w[n]w[n-R]/sum_n w[n]^2 diagnoses correlation, but periodogram correlation/variance depends on its square and on process assumptions. Never replace K by 'K independent averages' without an effective-DOF calculation or empirical trial audit.
stochastic_and_sample_conventions.statistics: Bias is E{Shat}-S; variance is E{|Shat-E{Shat}|^2}; MSE=variance+|bias|^2. The demo's CV is the across-seeded-trial sample SD divided by across-trial sample mean at a predeclared frequency/bin; report trial count (>=50) and the exact evaluation neighborhood.

psd_units_contract.canonical: Use the two-sided normalized-angular PSD on -pi<=omega<pi. Under the course transform pair, r_xx[0]=(1/(2 pi))integral S_xx(exp(j omega))domega. The ledger calls its values power per radians/sample; always print the dω/(2π) integration measure to remove normalization ambiguity.
psd_units_contract.white_noise_check: For zero-mean white noise of variance sigma_x^2, r_xx[ell]=sigma_x^2 delta[ell] and S_xx(exp(j omega))=sigma_x^2. Unit variance therefore plots flat at 1 in the canonical two-sided convention.
psd_units_contract.hz_conversion: With f=omega f_s/(2 pi), define S_xx,Hz(f)=S_xx(exp(j2 pi f/f_s))/f_s so integral from -f_s/2 to f_s/2 equals r_xx[0]. Thus unit-variance discrete white noise is flat at 1/f_s power/Hz.
psd_units_contract.one_sided_real: Only for real x[n], form a one-sided per-Hz PSD on 0<=f<=f_s/2 by doubling positive interior frequencies and leaving DC and, for even L, Nyquist undoubled. Its integral equals r_xx[0]. Do not apply this folding to complex/IQ data.
psd_units_contract.fft_estimator_scaling: Because the course forward FFT is unscaled, divide each two-sided modified periodogram by U=sum|w|^2 for the canonical angular normalization, or by f_s U for per-Hz density. Then apply the one-sided doubling rule only if requested. Do not divide by coherent gain C_w; C_w calibrates deterministic tone amplitude, while U calibrates noise power density.
psd_units_contract.display: A dB PSD is 10 log10(S/S_ref), never 20 log10. State S_ref and retain units as dB relative to one signal-unit^2/(Hz or canonical angular unit).

misconceptions.myth: A longer raw periodogram becomes stable because its expected value approaches the PSD.
misconceptions.replacement: Bias can shrink while variance stays of order S^2; consistency requires both to vanish.
misconceptions.discriminator: Repeat a fixed normalized bin across >=50 equal-length seeded white-noise trials as N grows, keeping padding separate from averaging.

misconceptions.myth: One realization's lag average is the ensemble expectation because the process is WSS.
misconceptions.replacement: WSS fixes first/second moments across time; ergodicity is the additional premise connecting long time averages to ensemble moments.
misconceptions.discriminator: Contrast white noise with a constant random variable across time: both can be WSS, but one realization of the latter never reveals the ensemble distribution.

misconceptions.myth: A deterministic impulse is white noise because both spectra are flat.
misconceptions.replacement: White noise is a stationary random-process model with zero nonzero-lag correlation; an impulse is a nonstationary deterministic sequence.
misconceptions.discriminator: Compare block autocorrelations: only the impulse-containing block is nonzero.

misconceptions.myth: Fifty-percent overlap doubles the independent evidence or guarantees the advertised variance reduction.
misconceptions.replacement: Overlap increases frame count while shared samples correlate estimates; window, hop, and process determine effective degrees of freedom.
misconceptions.discriminator: At fixed M and record length, compare empirical CV for nonoverlap, 50%, and heavier overlap and report both K and measured CV.

misconceptions.myth: Window normalization for a tone and for a PSD is the same.
misconceptions.replacement: Use C_w=sum w for deterministic amplitude and U=sum|w|^2 for noise-power density.
misconceptions.discriminator: Unit-variance white noise must average to 1 in the two-sided canonical PSD regardless of chosen window.

misconceptions.myth: A smoother Welch curve is unconditionally better.
misconceptions.replacement: Averaging spends segment length and broadens the effective spectral kernel; smoothing can merge the required 0.04-cycles/sample tone pair.
misconceptions.discriminator: The demo must satisfy tone separation and CV<0.30 simultaneously, not optimize visual smoothness.
